result.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials. Between sessions, an offline agent distills validated lessons, making the memory self-improving. On two ads models, Engram reaches the 32-trial result of a no-memory control with 47% fewer trials and also ends with a better model on average.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Engram，一个用于 LLM agent 自动调优异构模型的多阶段记忆系统：它把过往试验结果与背后的假设及理由关联，在初始引导、会话检索和候选审查三个决策点提供证据，并在会话间离线蒸馏已验证经验，使记忆自我改进。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「判定过往证据是否适用于当前模型」的检索与有效性筛选机制，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与跨样本经验复用提供类比线索，可供核查，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
